The four vectors in step 3.1 are an orthonormal set of four vectors in the four-dimensional space whose product basis is listed in [F4]; hence they are an orthonormal basis.

These four projections are self-adjoint idempotents, their ranges are pairwise orthogonal, and their sum is the identity because the eight orthonormal computational basis vectors from [F8] are partitioned by their first two bits. Hence they form a projective measurement as in [F2].

Write the post-gate vector in [F1] as $\Omega=\sum_i c_i e_i$ in the orthonormal basis [F4]. For the matrix $\rho$ with entries $\rho_{ij}=c_i\overline{c_j}$, self-adjointness is immediate; for any coordinate vector $z$, $\langle\rho z,z\rangle=|\sum_j z_j\overline{c_j}|^2\ge0$. The matrix [F6] sends $(\alpha,\beta)$ to $(\beta,\alpha)$ under $X$ and to $(\alpha,-\beta)$ under $Z$, so each preserves $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2$ and every $X^bZ^a$ preserves norm. The branch vectors in [F1] have orthogonal $AB$ labels, hence $\operatorname{tr}(\rho)=\sum_i|c_i|^2=\|\Omega\|^2=\|\psi\|^2=1$ by [A1] and [F7]. Thus $\rho$ is a density operator under the description in [F2].

By [F2] and [F7], the probability weight of label $(a,b)$ is $\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{ab})=|c_{ab0}|^2+|c_{ab1}|^2$, the sum of the two diagonal entries selected by $P_{ab}$. The branch vector in [F1] has these two coefficients equal to those of $\frac12X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$, so this sum is $\frac14\|X^bZ^a\psi\|^2$.

The matrices in [F6] are unitary: direct multiplication gives $X^*X=I$ and $Z^*Z=I$. Hence $\|X^bZ^a\psi\|^2=\|\psi\|^2=1$, so every weight in step 2.1 is $1/4$. By [F3] these are the outcome probabilities, and the four weights sum to one.
